speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether BCA is actively encouraging construction and infrastructure companies to use drones for inspections of projects, especially for the facades of high-rise buildings.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the Ministry is educating and equipping construction and infrastructure companies to utilise drone technology to increase efficiency and safety in the workplace.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) how has the use of drones by the building industry helped to improve productivity and effectiveness in building inspections, repairs and maintenance; and (b) whether the process of seeking approvals for the use of drones can be streamlined and the turnaround time for granting approvals improved.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State, if I could just interrupt, are you answering for the three questions?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Yes, Sir, if I could take Question Nos 35 to 37 together?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The Government has also been investing in research and development to advance facade inspection technologies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Beyond facade inspections, the Government is currently exploring how UAS can be used in building maintenance.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For example, agencies, such as Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA), Housing and Development Board (HDB) and JTC are exploring the potential of using UAS, in tandem with robotics, to undertake the cleaning of building facades.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As the use of UAS in building maintenance and repairs is nascent and has not been widely adopted in the industry, BCA will continue to partner the industry and research institutes to explore new use cases for UAS in the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the approvals required to use drones, BCA's approval is required for facade inspections where Competent Persons (CPs) intend to use technology, including the use of UAS.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: DSPs will also need to obtain the necessary permits from the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) prior to using UAS to carry out the inspections.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: CAAS will assess the safety of the UAS operations and coordinate the airspace for UAS activities.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: CAAS also leverages on information technology systems to better track and enhance the efficiency of processing approvals.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: To keep pace with the application of UAS across more use cases, CAAS will continue to review its regulations and processes with Government agencies to streamline the approval process for UAS activities without compromising aviation and public safety, as well as security.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned that under the "green lane", it will take three days to get the approval to use a drone.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: From my experiences with the contractors, some told me it took as long as two weeks to get approvals to be able to fly the drone.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether in cases like for very localised use for HDB heartlands just to inspect the HDB blocks, can a kind of blanket approval be given for the whole works, for example, repair and redecoration (R&R) work?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can approval be just given for the whole stretch rather than you need to go for a case-by-case approval in the use of the drones?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, it really depends on the DSPs that the CP assigns the work to.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So far, we have not come across significant issues around permit approvals for most of the cases that we have seen.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In Mr Liang's case, if there are specific issues that he or his Town Council has encountered, we will be happy to take it up and look at it.
